newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says budget deficit running at 2.9 pct/GDP.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says budget deficit running at 2.9 pct/GDP.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel was quoted on Monday as saying that Germany's budget deficit was currently running at 2.9 percent of GDP, putting Bonn on course to qualify for European monetary union.
When asked by the Munich Abendzeitung whether Germany would this year hit the three percent limit set by the Maastricht treaty, Waigel said: "We are currently below, actually at 2.9 percent."

Waigel was speaking after a mini-congress of his Christian Social Union (CSU) party passed a resolution late last week which set a strict definition of the deficit target under which qualification for Europe's single currency will be judged.

Waigel, who is CSU leader, backed the "three percent is 3.0 percent" resolution, which ended days of speculation that he was trying to distance himself from a strict interpretation because of Germany's own budget difficulties.

The six leading institutes whose forecasts underpin budget policy will predict a deficit of 3.2 percent this year when they publish their next outlook on April 22, the Berliner Zeitung newspaper reported. The institutes had forecast a deficit of 3.5 percent last autumn.
Waigel said that if unemployment -- which fell by 190,000 in March to 4.5 million -- rose further above forecasts further measures would have to be taken.
He said he still did not rule a freeze on supplementary government spending, "even though this is a double-edged sword because it also includes growth-promoting investments".
